totals.note: Announced ($592.1B) is the sum of the 13 priced rows on every basis, equal to the compute desk's total. Contracted ($455.7B) means a signed obligation with a stated dollar figure that is neither a ceiling nor unconfirmed. Of it, $217.9B is documented at T1 or T2 (AWS, Microsoft, the $34.5B of closed chip notes that the desk carves out of the Broadcom line, TeraWulf, Riot, RUM, Akamai) and $237.8B comes from prospectus coverage (Google $111.1B and the rest of the Broadcom-related line, $126.7B), which is T3 second-hand. Up to ($89.6B) is SpaceX, cancellable on 90 days' notice, and Nscale, conditional on its financing. Reported and unconfirmed ($46.8B) is Lambda, Volta and Akamai plan 1. GW 15.845 is 13.0 'up to' ceilings (AWS 5.0, Google 5.0, AMD 2.0, Microsoft 1.0) plus 2.845 of floors, IT load and press figures. Campus-level capacity that is not Anthropic's share is left out: Hut 8 Beacon Point 704 MW, RUM campus 250 MW, Project Rainier 2.2 GW, SpaceX fleet 1.4 GW. Not summed, as overlaps or non-commitments: the $50B Fluidstack program, Hut 8 River Bend $7.0B, the $10B Broadcom direct order, the $34.5B SPV notes, Rainier $11B, ERock power, and talks. Reconcile to the prospectus: $518.2B is Google 111.1 + Amazon 110.0 + Microsoft 31.4 + Broadcom-related leases 161.2 + SpaceX up to 84.5 + AMD over 20.0. The desk sum sits $73.9B above it. Four lines are lower in the desk table by 70.9: SpaceX -39.5, AMD -20.0 (the desk table has no AMD dollar figure), AWS -10.0, Microsoft -1.4. Seven names outside the six partners add 144.8: Nscale 44.6, Lambda 35.0, TeraWulf 19.0, RUM 13.7, Akamai 13.4, Volta 10.0, Riot 9.1. The Information's $517B is a maximum contract value for deals signed since Oct 2025 (T3), 0.2% below the prospectus total, and measures something else. Count the S-1 figure as the anchor for fixed obligations and the desk sum as the anchor for everything announced.

gross_margin_bridge_note: Estimate, tier T3 (modeled). No bar is a company disclosure. Unit: $1 of list-price revenue, 2026E at Q2 and Q3 2026 scale. Central gross margin is 73% of realized gross revenue (range 56% to 83%), or 66 cents per $1 of list, after cloud-partner share and before training and stock compensation. The partner share is deducted here although the prospectus books it as marketing expense, so the S-1 gross margin, when reported, may sit about 8 points higher. Three scopes stay separate. Company-adjusted above 80% is before partner share and before training (first memo bar, 81%). PitchBook's about 44% counts all compute including training and equals 1 minus $0.56 (second memo bar). The Information's -94% for FY2024 and about 40% for FY2025 count paying-user costs only, a prior-year scope not drawn. Reading $0.56 as all compute is an interpretation: it is the only reading that fits the FT's above 80%, because partner share of about 0.08 cannot close a 0.36 gap. Training and other compute is then at least $0.36 per revenue dollar in Q2 2026E. The reported path is -94% (FY2024), about 40% (FY2025), 63% (2027E, VERIFY) or above 70% (The Information) and 77% (2028E plan). The 2026E central of 73% already sits at the 2028 plan level, so either the plan was conservative (it predates the revenue surge) or its paying-user scope is narrower. Cache is sized outside the bars: if cache reads were billed at standard input rates, list-equivalent revenue would be about 3.5x to 5.5x realized (33% to 60% cache-read share of spend, inferred from Anthropic's Fable 5.1 cost claims), so uncached list price is a poor base. What would move the bars: batch and fast-mode volume and the Sep 2026 cache cuts (discounts); marketplace share, now 47% of sales (partner share); chip mix, utilization and the July end of SpaceX's ramp discount (inference); the S-1's cost of revenue, gross profit and free-tier cost (all bars). Bars add to the gross margin exactly.

what.t: Compute desk tally, Sep 30: $592.1B across 13 priced deals and 15.8 GW. $217.9B is firm and documented at T1 or T2. $89.6B is cancellable or conditional (SpaceX, Nscale). $46.8B is reported but unconfirmed. $237.8B comes from prospectus coverage only. 13.0 GW is 'up to'. Campus capacity that is not Anthropic's share (Beacon Point 704 MW, RUM 250 MW) is excluded. Anthropic has disclosed no total.

Reuters, Sep 29 (total T2, split T3): the draft prospectus shows at least $518B over about ten years with six partners, roughly 80% non-cancelable or payable regardless of use. Google $111.1B, Amazon $110B, Broadcom-related leases $161.2B, Microsoft $31.4B, SpaceX up to $84.5B, AMD over $20B. The lines sum to $518.2B. The S-1 is not public.

The Information, Sep 6 (T3): up to $517B of contracts signed since Oct 2025 and at least 14.8 GW on top of 1 to 2 GW already held. It is a maximum value with no partner split. It sits 0.2% below the prospectus total but measures something else. The $531B figure in the checklist appears in no source.

The desk sum is $73.9B above the prospectus sum. Four S-1 lines are higher than the desk's figures by $70.9B: SpaceX $39.5B, AMD $20.0B, AWS $10.0B, Microsoft $1.4B. Seven names outside the six partners add $144.8B: Nscale, Lambda, TeraWulf, RUM, Akamai, Volta and Riot. The record does not say why they sit outside.

SpaceX S-1 (T1): $1.25B a month through May 2029 for Colossus and Colossus II, terminable by either party on 90 days' notice, first two months discounted. Musk says the firm period is 180 days (T2). Prospectus coverage says up to $84.5B (T3). Firm exposure is 90 to 180 days of fees, $3.75B to $7.5B (derived), 8% to 17% of the $45B nominal.

Compute and infrastructure spend was $7.33B in FY2025, 58% of opex and $1.60 per revenue dollar (Reuters on the draft prospectus, T2). The ratio was $0.71 in Q1 2026 and is projected at $0.56 for Q2 (WSJ projections via PYMNTS, T3). Q2 revenue was $11.5B and run-rate passed $65B at end-July (Bloomberg, T2).

Gross margin comes in separate scopes. FY2024 at -94% counts paying-user costs only, and FY2025 at about 40% is about 38% with free-user inference (The Information, PitchBook, T3). PitchBook's about 44% for Q2 2026 is 1 minus $0.56 of compute per revenue dollar, scope unstated. The FT reports above 80% for Q2 and Q3 2026 before partner share and training (T3).

Funding has five layers. Equity raised is $124.3B (PitchBook ledger, Sep 30). Amazon has funded $18.0B and a $15.0B facility opens on AWS delivery milestones (10-Q, Jun 30). Lessors closed $34.5B of chip notes on Jun 9. A $15B pre-IPO revolver, an expansion of a $2.5B one, is reported near final. PitchBook counted the chip notes on Jul 16 ($161.254B total) and dropped them on Sep 30 ($126.754B).

means.t: About $414B of the $518B is non-cancelable or must-pay. Google, Amazon, Microsoft and the Broadcom-related leases sum to $413.7B, 79.8% of the named lines and 6.4x the $65B run-rate. Compute is a fixed charge, so margin depends on utilization as much as on price. Only the SpaceX line, up to $84.5B, is described as cancellable. AMD's terms are not stated.

Cost per GW-year depends on what is rented. Powered shells run $1.9B to $2.4B. TPU systems finance at up to $34.5B per GW, about $6.9B a year over a five-year lease. Vera Rubin rentals run $12.5B to $16.2B. SpaceX's fee works out at $21B to $50B. The building is 15% to 19% of a GPU rental dollar, so chip mix drives blended cost.

At the $65B end-July run-rate and an estimated 1.4 to 2.3 GW live, revenue is $28B to $46B per GW-year gross. Blended compute cost is $11B to $18B. Capacity must grow 7x to 11x to reach 15.8 GW, and holding $34B per GW needs about $540B of run-rate. The forecasts in the record imply $12B to $23B per GW.

Amazon's 'up to $20B more' is a facility that opens as AWS hits compute-delivery milestones (10-Q, T1). Amazon has funded $18.0B and Anthropic owes AWS more than $100B, so both legs are in the record. AMD pairs up to $5B of equity with over $20B of compute. Akamai and RUM issue warrants to Anthropic. No filing traces cash from one leg to the other.

The margin figures reconcile once scopes are separated. At $0.56 of compute per revenue dollar in Q2 and a company margin above 80% before partner share and training, inference is at most $0.20 and training and other compute at least $0.36. The bridge's central 73% (range 56% to 83%) is after partner share and before training. Reading $0.56 as all compute is an interpretation.

Training sits outside the company's gross margin and inside the stricter breakeven. Adjusted operating profit before training was first positive in Q2 2026 (FT, T3). Profitability with training as cost of goods sold is put at 2028 to 2029 by secondary WSJ summaries (T4). The WSJ Q2 projection reportedly includes training (T5 commentary); the FT measure does not, so the two margins may not share a scope.

Counterparty concentration is high. Google-linked TPU supply (Google Cloud plus Broadcom-related leases) is 52.6% of the S-1 lines, Amazon 21.2%, SpaceX 16.3%, Microsoft 6.1%, AMD 3.9%. Amazon and Google also carried 47% of FY2025 sales. Google backstops lessors with exposure up to about $44B (FT, T3). The flexible supplier, SpaceX, is also a rival.

implications.t: Underwrite $413.7B as fixed charges and $104.5B as options. Commitment-implied payments on straight-line schedules: 2026 $28B to $31B, 2027 $43B to $87B (base $62B), 2028 $53B to $106B (base $80B, 41% of Reuters' $190B to $200B revenue forecast). Treat these as estimates until the S-1 shows obligations by year.

Next four quarters (Q4 2026 to Q3 2027): commitment-implied payments of $40B to $75B, base $56B, 2.2x Q2's annualized compute cost of $25.8B. Capacity lands before revenue. SpaceX's ramp discount was due to end in July (T5 commentary), and the company warned infrastructure spending could stop profit lasting the year (WSJ via PYMNTS, T3). Holding $0.56 needs about $100B of annualized revenue by mid-2027 on the base schedule.

Watch these. SpaceX exit or repricing (13% to 21% of live capacity on 90 days' notice). Nscale's Qualifying Financing. Amazon facility use beyond the $5.0B Series H purchase. A second ~$36B chip package. AMD's first GW in 1H 2027. Q3 adjusted operating income, expected positive. Whether the S-1 defines gross margin before or after training.

Keep debt and equity apart. The $34.5B chip notes are lessor debt; Anthropic's liability is the lease stream inside the $161.2B line. PitchBook's total moves by $34.5B with the treatment. A second package would take SPV financing to about $70.5B. Against $413.7B of non-cancelable wording stand about $50B of new Series H cash, a $15B revolver reported near final and an IPO reported at up to $100B.

List-price deflation is the main threat to revenue per GW. Opus list fell 73% in 14 months and cache reads are 2.5% to 5% of input on the newest models. Simple payback on a TPU-class GW is 1.5 years at today's revenue per GW and about 4 years at the $12B implied by Reuters' 2028 forecast, against a five-year lease. Second-order: price cuts land before capacity costs fall.

Diversification is real and costly: Claude runs on three hyperscaler clouds, four chip families and 15 named counterparties. Yet Google-linked supply is 52.6%, and NVIDIA sits under Azure, SpaceX, Nscale, Lambda, Volta and RUM. No owned data center or chip inventory appears in the record; custom silicon hiring and ERock's 470 MW power order are the only owned-asset signals. Second-order: lessors, hosts and vendor equity marks carry Anthropic demand risk.

second_order: Vendors mark up their Anthropic stakes as rounds reprice (Amazon carries $190.4B against $18.0B at cost), and those gains sit beside the compute Anthropic buys from them. An IPO near $2T re-marks again, and a slip or a down round re-marks the vendors too.

Google-backed lessors and hosts carry Anthropic counterparty risk. Google's exposure is up to about $44B (FT, T3), and a shortfall would surface first at Broadcom's residual-value backstop, the second-lien B notes and small-cap hosts. Broadcom's 8-K says consumption depends on Anthropic's continued commercial success.

A second ~$36B chip package would put lessor financing near $70.5B, more than 40% of the $161.2B lease line. How rating agencies, PitchBook and the S-1 classify it changes the reported debt load by that amount without changing the obligation.

Milestone gating correlates failure. Amazon's facility, AMD's equity, Google's $30B and Nscale's financing all open on delivery or targets, so a delivery slip delays capital and capacity together, while a demand slip hits the non-cancelable core and supplier equity marks at once.

Duration mismatch. Shells run 20 years (TeraWulf, Riot), GPU services six years (Nscale, Volta, RUM) and chip leases five years (SPV), so one shell outlives several chip cycles. Amodei cited GPU depreciation and timing risk on Dec 3, 2025. Obsolescence and refinancing risk sit with Anthropic or its guarantors.
Custom silicon would lower the chip share (81% to 85% of a GPU rental dollar) but adds design and fab commitments that are not in the record.

uncertainties.note: This file and model.json read PitchBook's $0.56 differently. The model treats it as inference-only (2026 gross margin 48%) and adds $13.0B of training, so its 2026 cost of revenue plus training is $42.0B, 75% of revenue. Read as all compute, 2026 is about $32.0B to $37.9B. If it is inference-only, the FT's above 80% cannot hold.
uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The S-1 cost of revenue line with a training split, or a dollar figure for Q3 adjusted operating income with a bridge.

uncertainties.what_would_change_it: The S-1 operating-income reconciliation and its adjustments.
